claims.text: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran is fully prepared if the war with the United States resumes.
The United States rejected Tehran's seven-day roadmap to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump stated he expects more talks with Iran during the week of September 28, 2026.
US President Donald Trump claimed that Washington is going to win the war with Iran very soon.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it seized a US underwater drone in the Strait of Hormuz, identifying it as an Mk 18 Mod 2 Kingfish.
IRGC spokesperson Second Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi confirmed on X the capture of an American Mk 18 Mod 2 Kingfish autonomous AUV in the Strait of Hormuz.
The IRGC had previously identified the captured underwater platform as a REMUS 600.
The IRGC declared that the Strait of Hormuz is closed and warned of relentless action against unauthorized maritime traffic.
Iranian officials presented a proposal at the UN General Assembly in New York for a seven-day truce followed by the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump told Axios regarding Iran, 'They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make.'
US President Donald Trump told Axios that Iranian negotiators 'overplayed their hand.'
The conflict between Washington and Tehran began nearly seven months prior to September 2026 when the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran.
Iran's foreign minister stated that Iran's proposal called for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East, including in Lebanon.
US UN Ambassador Mike Waltz described Iran's proposal as a cynical attempt to ask for the release of sanctions and access to billions in assets just to talk.
Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in June 2026 to end the war, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and launch nuclear talks.
IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebi stated via Tasnim news agency that Iran will not stop punishing the US until its seven conditions are met.
IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebi told AFP that ending hostilities in Yemen was among Tehran's demands.
US UN Ambassador Mike Waltz told CNN that the US rejected Iran's proposal because Iranian negotiators were asking for everything up front.
US President Donald Trump stated on September 26, 2026, that the US was winning tremendously and had total control of the Hormuz strait.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told CBS that Iran is ready for talks on its nuclear program but will not accept bullying or coercion.
Mike Waltz stated US President Donald Trump raised concerns with Chinese President Xi Jinping regarding alleged Chinese assistance in Iranian missile targeting.
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic resigned on September 27, 2026, to run for prime minister in the October 25 snap parliamentary election.
Aleksandar Vucic handed over presidential duties to Parliament Speaker Ana Brnabic, who will serve as acting president.
Aleksandar Vucic is constitutionally barred from seeking a third term as Serbian president.
Protests in Serbia were triggered by the November 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people.
Aleksandar Vucic pardoned 49 people before leaving office, including 23 linked to cases arising from protests.
Aleksandar Vucic is seeking the prime minister nomination on the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) ballot.
A student-led movement in Serbia is contesting the parliamentary election under the banner 'Students Win'.
The 'Students Win' movement is contesting the election with the backing of several opposition parties, including the Democratic Party.
Official statistics show the average net monthly salary in Serbia was 1,032 euros ($1,174) in April 2026, compared with 1,555 euros ($1,770) in neighbouring Croatia.
Under Serbia's constitution, presidential elections must be held no more than three months after a president's resignation.
The October parliamentary election pits Vucic's Progressive Party against Students Win and a pro-Western coalition called European Serbia.
Aleksandar Vucic became prime minister of Serbia in 2014 before being elected president in 2017.
In Serbia, the prime minister is formally more powerful than the president under the country's constitution.
Serbia's independent Bureau for Social Research filed a complaint alleging that Vucic abused a public institution as president to promote his party.
Aleksandar Vucic told state television RTS that foreign powers and unidentified internal groups planned to stir unrest on election night.
Aleksandar Vucic stated that the first round of Serbia's presidential election will take place by the end of December.
South African police discovered the body of an 11th woman in an open field in Ekurhuleni municipality near Johannesburg.
The body of a semi-naked woman, who appeared to have been stoned to death, was found near a cemetery in Ekurhuleni on September 26, 2026.
South African police arrested a man almost 400km away in connection with the woman's body found on September 26, bringing total arrests in the case series to four.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa stated that the ongoing killings of women are a shame on the men of South Africa.
South Africa has an average of 15 women killed per day.
Seventeen people were killed and 15 injured when eight gunmen attacked a bar near Johannesburg on Saturday evening.
Ten people were killed and 11 injured in a separate mass shooting outside an entertainment venue near Cape Town early Sunday morning.
Gauteng Police Commissioner Lt Gen Tommy Mthombeni stated that victims of the Johannesburg shooting included citizens of Ethiopia, Lesotho, and South Africa.
Eleven people were killed days prior to the weekend shootings when gunmen attacked a house in KwaMakhutha township near Durban.
South Africa records about 60 murders per day in a population of 62 million.
The bar shooting near Johannesburg occurred in Wedela township, about 50 miles southwest of central Johannesburg.
Gunmen in Wedela were armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols, stole cellphones from patrons, and torched two vehicles.
The shooting near Cape Town took place at a shisanyama venue in Lwandle at approximately 1:46am on Sunday.
Five people died at the scene at Lwandle, and five others died in hospital from their injuries.
South Africa had a murder rate of almost 40 per 100,000 people in 2024, ranking ninth-highest globally.
More than 22,700 people were murdered in South Africa in the 12 months leading up to June 30.
In June 2026, 12 people were killed in a mass shooting at an informal settlement in Johannesburg linked to illegal gold miners.
A local farmer in Whelford called 999 at around 1am on Sunday after noticing three white vans and a group of hooded, balaclava-wearing men.
Police arrived on the scene in Whelford 15 minutes after the emergency call was made.
Police evacuated residents from 85 households in Whelford to a nearby leisure centre in Cirencester at 6am on Sunday.
RAF Fairford features a 2-mile runway reinforced to support heavy bombers such as B-1 and B-52 aircraft used in attacks on Iran.
Five men were arrested near RAF Fairford in the UK on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences.
US and UK leaders stated the five arrested men were under investigation and planning to cause big damage.
Gloucestershire police received a report at 12:45am local time regarding three suspicious white vans travelling towards RAF Fairford.
Army bomb disposal robots were deployed on Sunday afternoon to examine the three white vans.
US President Donald Trump called the arrests fantastic, stating that the suspects were looking to do big damage.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned in July that any UK base used in strikes against Iran would be a legitimate target.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree accused Saudi Arabia of conducting two air raids on a market on the outskirts of Taiz.
Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV reported that a Saudi air strike on a market in Taiz killed seven people and wounded 40, including five children.
Multiple Houthi sources told AFP that nearly 30 Houthi fighters and eight civilians were killed in a series of strikes.
Houthis launched an offensive in September that seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
Saudi Arabia stated it intercepted two Houthi drones heading toward Riyadh on Saturday.
Fighting near Taiz escalated after Houthi forces captured the strategic Red Sea port of Mokha on September 10, 2026.
Taiz is Yemen's third largest city with a population close to one million people.
Yemen's armed forces reported carrying out 756 operations against Houthi positions over 72 hours, killing or wounding 2,316 Houthi members.
Yemeni military officials claimed four Iranian experts specializing in drone and missile operations were killed in Taiz governorate.
Yemeni military sources told Reuters that Houthi fighters had recently established a military camp near the market targeted in Taiz.
A nor'easter storm brought coastal flooding, heavy rain, and strong winds from Virginia to Maine.
States of emergency were declared in New York and New Jersey in response to the nor'easter storm.
Leighton Brown, a 56-year-old NYC Housing Authority employee, was killed by a falling tree in east Brooklyn.
More than 160,000 households across the northeastern US lost power due to the storm.
FlightAware recorded over 2,400 flight delays and 1,199 cancellations on Saturday.
The Global Citizen Festival in Central Park and Ed Sheeran's concert at Gillette Stadium were cancelled due to the severe weather.
Some areas in New Jersey received more than 4 inches (10cm) of rain from Friday through the weekend.
More than 250 flights were cancelled at Boston Logan International Airport as wind gusts reached 64 km/h (40 mph).
New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency covering eight counties including the Bronx, Kings, Queens, and Westchester.
FlightAware reported more than 5,000 US flight delays and nearly 550 cancellations nationwide during the weekend storm.
Moderate coastal flooding occurred at the Battery on the southern tip of Manhattan on Saturday night.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated that the city spent one-third of the year facing flood threats.
Nor'easters are large cyclones in the western North Atlantic Ocean that form off the east coast of the United States.
Up to 5 inches (13 cm) of rain was forecast for areas of Massachusetts, equivalent to more than a month's worth of rain.
More than 70% of Swiss voters rejected a referendum proposal for a stricter definition of national neutrality.
The rejected proposal would have barred Switzerland from imposing sanctions without UN approval and prevented closer ties with NATO.
The referendum initiative was supported by the right-wing Swiss People's Party (SVP) and opposed by the federal government and major parties.
Switzerland was internationally recognized as neutral in 1815 at the Congress of Vienna and defined by the Hague Convention of 1907.
The proposal for strict neutrality failed across all Swiss cantons in the referendum.
SVP backer Christoph Blocher spent an estimated 2 million Swiss francs (€2.1m) funding the strict neutrality campaign.
Opponents noted that Switzerland has cooperated with NATO for 30 years despite not being a member of the alliance.
